title: No way to select silenced audio and video elements by state
title_original: Add new selectors and move some existing selectors out of experimental
text_original:
- Add `:open` and `:muted`
- Recognize `:autofill`, `:buffering`, `:fullscreen`, `:picture-in-picture`, `:popover-open`, `:seeking`, `:stalled`, and `:volume-locked`.
- Move various existing pseudo-classes out of experimental status.
text_rewritten:
We audit saved pages for media that is embedded with sound switched off. The CSS Level 4 state pseudo-class for that, :muted, is refused as an unsupported pseudo-class, so the pattern will not compile at all and we are left with the attribute test [muted] -- which also picks up unrelated elements that happen to carry a muted attribute in generated markup.

Please support :muted so that it selects exactly the audio and video elements that are silenced. It has to work on its own, narrowed to one element type (video:muted, audio:muted), and nested inside :not() and :is(). Attribute-presence selectors such as [muted] must keep their current, broader meaning.
body:
We audit saved pages for media that is embedded with sound switched off. The CSS Level 4 state pseudo-class for that, :muted, is refused as an unsupported pseudo-class, so the pattern will not compile at all and we are left with the attribute test [muted] -- which also picks up unrelated elements that happen to carry a muted attribute in generated markup.

Please support :muted so that it selects exactly the audio and video elements that are silenced. It has to work on its own, narrowed to one element type (video:muted, audio:muted), and nested inside :not() and :is(). Attribute-presence selectors such as [muted] must keep their current, broader meaning.
acceptance_hint: :muted compiles and selects only silenced audio and video elements, composes inside :not() and :is(), and [muted] still matches every element that merely carries the attribute.
